pull_requests.head: feat/session-teaching-mode
pull_requests.title: Add reversible Guided and Explain teaching styles
pull_requests.body:
Learners can now choose Guided or Explain from a reversible session toolbar control. Guided mode asks for one reasoning step at a time and keeps committed answers and unselected correct-option indicators hidden until explicitly revealed, addressing the existing predict-then-immediately-explain behavior.

The choice is local to the session, survives reload, applies to the next reply, and is preserved when changing models. Existing sessions retain their prior behavior until a choice is made. The code audit and model-behavior evaluation limits are documented in docs/teaching-diagnosis.md.

Validation: all 1,907 existing and new tests passed; TypeScript and architectural lint passed. A real local-server smoke test switched Guided → Explain → Guided, verified stored settings and rendered the toolbar. Deterministic tests verify UI/prompt plumbing; live-model adherence and retention gains have not been measured. The optimized production build and supported standalone startup have since passed on the complete review stack.


Adversarial review fixed Guided partial-multi-select answer indicators. PR CI now runs the full quality suite and native standalone checks on Windows only. Both checks passed on the reviewed head. Tablet-specific fixes in #23 are not dependencies of this PR.

pull_requests.head: feat/multimodal-learning-evidence
pull_requests.title: Capture sketches, dictation and code as question evidence
pull_requests.body:
Sketches/images, code snapshots, and accompanying typed or dictated reasoning now reach the agent together on normal messages, question answers and practice submissions. Images are native provider content, with question/problem identity preserved; code and reported output are explicitly learner evidence. The practice dock now flushes pending dictation before submitting.

Adapted image transport and validation from upstream LearnHarness PR #263 (AGPL-3.0), excluding PDF support. Added bounded input/signature validation, image-model refusal before write-ahead persistence, local transcript previews, optimistic-record absorption and explicit selection/removal controls. Source provenance and remaining reuse candidates are documented in docs/reuse-provenance.md.

Validation: all 1,917 tests passed; TypeScript and architectural lint passed. New tests exercise image-selection/removal UI, serialization/replay, question-result and practice-message transport, and an actual agent turn through the injected provider adapter. Live paid-provider vision interpretation, microphone hardware and physical iPad input were not tested.

Stacked on feat/session-teaching-mode; this diff contains only multimodal learning evidence.

pull_requests.head: feat/quant-arithmetic-arena
pull_requests.title: Add a configurable mental arithmetic arena
pull_requests.body:
Adds a Mental arithmetic arena accessible from Quant training in the sidebar: configurable operations/ranges/duration, keyboard rounds, wrong-attempt retries, persisted seeded questions and absolute deadlines, reload recovery, history, accuracy, throughput and per-operation solve times.

Question generation is adapted from MIT-licensed YYZ-CR/zetamac-trainer (e810415), retaining its notice and using LearnHarness-local storage rather than its external services. Questions and verdicts are computed from stored seeds/settings; stale completed-question submissions cannot count twice. Shared training records use atomic replacement and refuse unsupported schema versions.

Validation: seven domain/storage/API tests passed; TypeScript and architectural lint passed. Real local HTTP checks and Chromium verified configuration, wrong/correct answers, Enter submission, score updates, reload recovery and stopping a round. Temporary smoke records were removed. No model key is required. Scores are local practice evidence, not an anti-cheat ranking.

Stacked on feat/multimodal-learning-evidence; this diff adds arithmetic and its training navigation/storage foundation.

pull_requests.head: feat/cpp-workspace
pull_requests.title: Add a persistent multi-file C++ learning workspace
pull_requests.body:
Adds a persistent multi-file C++ workspace with locally served Monaco, problem notes, standard input, explicit saves, tab-local draft recovery, stale-tab conflict protection and save-as-copy. Selected source files can be staged as frozen evidence in an existing or new teaching session, where the learner adds typed/dictated reasoning and submits through the normal answer loop.

Uses MIT-licensed Monaco packages with locked versions and self-hosted assets prepared by postinstall; no editor CDN is required. Source/run evidence follows upstream LearnHarness PR #241. Compilation is implemented in its separate feature PR rather than advertised by this workspace change.

Validation: workspace/evidence tests (15) passed; TypeScript and architectural lint passed; asset preparation ran twice. Chromium verified local Monaco loading without CDN requests, editing, saving, reload recovery and selected-file handoff into a real session draft. Temporary workspace/session records were removed.

Stacked on feat/quant-arithmetic-arena.

pull_requests.head: feat/isolated-cpp-runner
pull_requests.title: Compile and test C++20 in disposable bounded containers
pull_requests.body:
Connects the C++ workspace to an authenticated local compiler worker: C++20 compilation, stdin, warnings/errors, optional sanitizers, test-case comparisons, cancellation and persisted source/output reports. A report can be brought into a teaching session together with the frozen source that produced it, even after later edits.

Adapts the report contract from upstream LearnHarness PR #241. Execution uses a digest-pinned official GCC image in disposable non-root containers with no network or host mounts, read-only root filesystems, CPU/memory/process/file/output limits and bounded compile/run durations. There is no host-execution fallback. The worker remains loopback-only and its token is never sent to the browser.

Validation: all 1,931 deterministic tests passed; TypeScript and architectural lint passed. Seven real-container integration tests passed, covering multiple files/stdin/checks, compiler errors, host isolation, time/output limits, sanitizers, auth, cancellation and cleanup. Chromium verified actual compilation/output and the frozen-source handoff after editing. Installation/startup instructions were saved in the cloud configuration draft; processes must restart after restoration.

Stacked on feat/cpp-workspace.


Adversarial review fixed draft preservation, send acknowledgment/retry handling, and runner evidence metadata. Regression checks, the full Windows quality suite, and the native standalone build passed on the reviewed head. Tablet-specific fixes in #23 are not dependencies of this PR.

pull_requests.head: feat/session-scratchpad
pull_requests.title: Add persistent session scratchpads with explicit tutor capture
pull_requests.body:
Adds persistent session/question-linked scratch work using Excalidraw's pen, eraser, shapes/text, undo/redo and pan/zoom, with independent pages, autosave, local draft recovery and stale-device conflict protection. An explicit capture stages a real PNG snapshot and origin references in the session's answer/composer, where it can be submitted with typed or dictated reasoning. Later edits do not change submitted images.

Embeds MIT-licensed Excalidraw with locally served assets. Code and bundled font notices are retained. The drawing surface disables image/import/embed tools; this feature focuses on learner scratch work rather than PDF support. Source references also identify workspace and execution snapshots.

Validation: all 1,936 deterministic tests passed; TypeScript and architectural lint passed. Chromium verified pen drawing, autosave, undo/redo, reload recovery, a valid PNG capture and answer-draft handoff, without drawing CDN requests. Physical Apple Pencil pressure/palm rejection is not yet verified; paired iPad access is a separate feature.

Based on main after merging #8–12.

Adversarial review fixed unsaved-draft loss when switching scratchpads. Saved-pad drafts and new unsaved pads remain recoverable; switching is refused while work is unsaved and local recovery storage is full, and becomes available after the server acknowledges a save. The production regression covers rapid switching, failed autosaves, and storage quota failure.

The corrected #13–18 stack passes 1,975 default tests, nine production-browser checks, TypeScript, ESLint, optimized build, standalone packaging/startup, and real HTTPS pairing. pull_requests.head: feat/ipad-companion
pull_requests.title: Pair an iPad with a scoped HTTPS scratch companion
pull_requests.body:
Pair an iPad browser with one LearnHarness scratch page through a dedicated HTTPS companion. Single-use two-minute codes grant eight-hour page-scoped access; acknowledged sequences support reconnect/replay, and offline drafts merge strokes and newer deletions. The PC receives drawing updates through the existing event stream and can capture them as question evidence.

Desktop editing pauses during pairing, with a visible Disconnect control that restores editing even if the helper is offline. The helper serves only companion assets and scoped drawing routes; private app control credentials remain server-side. Windows trusted HTTPS and Safari setup are documented in docs/ipad-companion.md. Excalidraw and its font fallback are bundled locally.

Validation: 1,940 regression tests; typecheck and architectural lint; real certificate-verified HTTPS integration; Chromium pairing, pen stroke, PC sync, reload and disconnect. Physical iPad/Pencil behavior remains unverified. Stacked on feat/session-scratchpad.

Adversarial review backported the tablet fixes into this feature: reserve a pad during concurrent pairing, abort/reset old transport generations on re-pairing, match Windows font chunk paths, and serve the linked drawing/font notices. Real certificate-verified HTTPS and production-browser regressions cover replay, isolation, offline recovery, delayed acknowledgments, touch input, and PC reclaim.

pull_requests.head: feat/estimation-confidence
pull_requests.title: Train estimation and confidence calibration
pull_requests.body:
Add an estimation trainer for products, roots, natural logs, birthday probabilities and assumption-based Fermi questions. Learners commit an estimate, 80% interval and explanation before references become available. Saved immutable attempts support resume/review, multiplicative error, interval scoring and aggregate calibration; Fermi scenarios are excluded from exact-reference calibration.

Validation: 5 mathematical/server tests; actual Chromium commit-before-reveal and persisted review; typecheck and lint. See docs/estimation-trainer.md for score interpretation. Stacked on feat/ipad-companion.

Adversarial review fixed accepted subnormal estimates producing non-finite log scores and crashing result rendering after JSON serialization. Scores now use a stable difference of logarithms and explicitly report factor overflow. Unit and production-browser regressions cover the original input.

pull_requests.head: feat/mistake-notebook
pull_requests.title: Diagnose recorded mistakes and demonstrate corrections
pull_requests.body:
The mistake notebook preserves completed source attempts, learner diagnoses, corrections, and original/variant retry history. Adversarial review now covers exams completed by the server deadline, including when the exam page was never reopened; catastrophically wrong finite estimates remain candidates even when their wide interval covers the reference.

Retries hide reference-derived tolerances until commitment. Demonstration proof is bound to the correction revision, so an earlier retry cannot prove a later edit when timestamps collide. Pending mutations freeze editable fields to prevent silent text loss.

Validation: targeted source/proof/metadata regressions and production HTTP/browser checks passed. The final reviewed stack passes 1,997 default tests, 27 production-browser checks, 58 production HTTP requests, typecheck/lint, optimized build, packaging/startup, real Docker judge/isolation workflows, and trusted HTTPS pairing. PR CI retains all quality and native standalone gates on Windows only. #19 is based on main after merging #13–18.

pull_requests.head: feat/spaced-retrieval

pull_requests.body:

Adversarial validation covers concurrent duplicate ratings, stale revisions, unsupported review modes, invalid snooze bounds, uncommitted ratings, and feedback restoration. Pending recall inputs are frozen while submission is awaiting acknowledgment. Retry answer metadata and correction-revision fixes are inherited from #19.

Validation: scheduler/core, production HTTP/browser, and full-stack checks passed: 1,997 default tests and 27 production-browser checks, with no skips. The complete review also exercised 58 production HTTP requests, real Docker/HTTPS workflows, typecheck/lint, optimized build, and standalone startup. pull_requests.head: feat/cpp-challenge-judge

pull_requests.body:
The C++ challenge judge runs frozen source against server-owned example/hidden checks in the isolated worker. Hidden runtime streams are redacted before reports are persisted or returned; caller-supplied test overrides cannot replace the challenge cases.

Real Docker tests accept general collision/top-k/variance solutions, reject example hardcoding, redact hidden-input echo and output floods, preserve frozen source, and avoid publishing completed reports for cancelled requests.
